library_preparation_preflight.summary: spring-modulith-events-core ships real classes but its EventPublicationAutoConfiguration only activates DefaultEventPublicationRegistry, PersistentApplicationEventMulticaster, and CompletionRegisteringAdvisor when a concrete EventPublicationRepository bean is present (@ConditionalOnBean). The -core artifact deliberately omits that implementation (it lives in sibling spring-modulith-events-jdbc/-jpa/-mongodb, none of which are dependencies here), so a generated test that just imports -core without supplying one will boot a context where the registry/advisor/multicaster never wire up, leaving the module's most reflection-heavy code unreached.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: In the generated test's Spring configuration, register a hand-written in-memory EventPublicationRepository bean (backed by a List/Map, implementing create/markCompleted/findIncompletePublications/deletePublications etc.) so EventPublicationAutoConfiguration's @ConditionalOnBean(EventPublicationRepository.class) condition is satisfied and DefaultEventPublicationRegistry, PersistentApplicationEventMulticaster, and CompletionRegisteringAdvisor actually get created. Then publish a domain event through the context and assert it is tracked/completed via EventPublicationRegistry to exercise the AOP completion-advisor and multicaster paths. No database, broker, or Docker image is needed — the repository interface is small enough to fake directly in test code, matching how spring-modulith's own unit tests exercise this module in isolation. No special system properties are needed; spring.modulith.events.externalization.enabled already defaults to true.
risks: If the test only instantiates plain POJOs (TargetEventPublication, PublicationTargetIdentifier) without booting a Spring context with the fake repository bean, coverage will look fine superficially but will miss the auto-configuration, AOP advisor, and multicaster classes entirely.
The optional io.namastack:namastack-outbox-api dependency is unrelated to core registry coverage and should not be added.
